title: Connection admission shim and idempotency fallthrough to mitigate 5xx and timeout waves
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: During a recent multi-tenant escalation we observed correlated 5xx responses and long tail timeouts originating from a mix of long-running streaming requests and aggressive client SDK retries. Root cause is a combination of head-of-line blocking on HTTP/2 multiplexed connections, a connection admission imbalance between proxy and runtime, and retry amplification when clients retried without idempotency semantics. This ticket implements a short-term admission shim + idempotency fallthrough to stop amplification and provide a graceful fallback path while longer-term fixes (connection pool redesign + kernel scheduling improvements) are developed.
impact_and_symptoms: Multiple paying customers reported intermittent 5xx spikes and cascading timeouts during a tenant burst window. Symptoms: elevated p50->p99 latency, surge in inflight requests per connection, frequent stream resets (RST_STREAM), and tens of thousands of duplicate model invocations due to SDK retries without idempotency keys. Observable in dashboards: edge/proxy connection saturation chart, runtime-inflight-per-connection heatmap, and cost spike in token processing for affected tenants.
proposed_fix_summary: 1) Admission shim at proxy layer that enforces per-connection and per-tenant soft slots with fast-path for idempotent single-shot requests. 2) Enforce and propagate an 'Idempotency-Key' header for streaming and unary calls; server will dedupe in-flight identical keys and fast-fail concurrent duplicates. 3) Introduce 'fallthrough routing' that sends excess requests to a lower-cost, short-context model variant (quantized/shorter-seq) instead of dropping. 4) Short-term SDK advisory to honor 429/503 with exponential backoff + jitter and to populate idempotency keys for retries. 5) Telemetry: emit admission decision events and idempotency dedupe metrics to reduce blast radius and measure impact.
acceptance_criteria: Proxy admission shim deployed to canary region and limiting per-connection inflight to configured soft slots
Server-side idempotency dedupe implemented for streaming endpoints with <50ms dedupe path overhead
Fallthrough routing returns 200 or controlled degrade response with clear headers for >95% of shaped requests (no silent drops)
Observed >60% reduction in duplicate model invocations during synthetic tenant burst tests
SDK advisory published and PRs merged with retry/backoff guidance
technical_notes_and_tradeoffs:
- Dedupe table will be a transient in-memory window keyed by (tenant, idempotency-key, route) and will expire after 30s. This avoids durable storage but does not protect post-restart duplicates.
- Admission shim is soft (requeue/shape) rather than hard drop to minimize customer-visible errors. There is a cost tradeoff: fallthrough routing increases unit cost but avoids 5xx cascades.
- We accept a small added latency on dedupe path (~20-50ms) for significantly lower downstream load.
- Longer-term: connection pool redesign and kernel scheduling improvements to be tracked in separate initiative (runtime-connpool-redesign).
rollback_plan: If canary shows increased customer errors or regressions, revert admission shim and idempotency enforcement flags via feature toggles. Immediately enable circuit-breaker to fast-fail non-priority tenants and route traffic to safe-mode small-quantized model. Notify SRE and customer success channel for manual interventions.
implementation_steps: Proxy: implement admission shim with configurable soft_slots and per-tenant weights
Runtime: add idempotency-key header parsing and in-memory dedupe window
Routing: implement fallthrough policy and route table entries for short-context model variants
SDK: publish advisory + add idempotency-key helper in official SDKs
Observability: add 'admission.decision' event, 'dedupe.hit' metric, and dashboard tiles
Canary rollout: region us-west-2 small subset (5% traffic) -> monitor 72h -> ramp
test_plan: 1) Unit tests for dedupe logic and admission enforcement. 2) Integration test that simulates HTTP/2 multiplexed clients with concurrent retries to validate dedupe and admission. 3) Load test: synthetic tenant surge (10x normal qps) in staging to measure duplicate invocations and latency under shim on/off. 4) Chaos: restart runtime during in-flight dedupe window to validate behavior and observability.
customer_communication_notes: Draft message for CS: explain short-term shaping and fallthrough to maintain availability, include guidance for clients to add idempotency keys and upgrade SDKs. Status page entries: post-mortem notes and guidance once RCA validated.
